candidates.title: A Clinical Insight into Von Hippel-Lindau Syndrome: Diagnostic Challenges.
candidates.abstract: Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) syndrome is a rare hereditary disorder characterised by the development of multiple benign and malignant tumours across various organs. Caused by mutations in the VHL tumour suppressor gene, it presents a wide range of clinical manifestations, including retinal haemangioblastomas, central nervous system tumours, renal cell carcinoma, pancreatic lesions, and phaeochromocytomas. This report describes the case of a 35-year-old woman who presented with visual impairment and abdominal masses. Imaging revealed typical VHL manifestations, including bilateral renal lesions and pancreatic involvement. Genetic testing confirmed the diagnosis. The patient underwent staged partial nephrectomies, with histopathology confirming clear cell renal cell carcinoma in both kidneys. This case highlights the importance of recognising the variable clinical and radiological presentations of VHL syndrome. Early diagnosis and multidisciplinary management are essential to reduce morbidity and mortality. Increased awareness and regular surveillance are critical for timely detection and intervention in patients with VHL syndrome.

candidates.title: When Appearances Deceive: A Silent Somatotroph Macroadenoma Presenting With Acromegaloid Features and Paradoxically Low Insulin-Like Growth Factor-1.
candidates.abstract: Silent somatotroph adenomas are uncommon pituitary neuroendocrine tumours (PitNETs) of the PIT1 lineage that express growth hormone (GH) immunohistochemically but without biochemical evidence of acromegaly. We report the case of a 32-year-old male patient referred with recurrent epistaxis, headache, right-sided diplopia, and third cranial nerve palsy. Clinical examination revealed acromegaloid features including frontal bossing, spade-like hands, and coarse facies, which were strongly suggestive of longstanding GH excess. However, preoperative insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) was paradoxically low at 13.1 nmol/L (reference range 15.5-33.1 nmol/L), creating a striking clinical-biochemical discordance. MRI demonstrated a giant sellar and suprasellar mass with chiasmal compression, right cavernous sinus invasion, and extension into the paranasal sinuses. The patient underwent endoscopic transsphenoidal resection. Neuropathology confirmed a densely granulated PIT1-lineage somatotroph adenoma with scattered GH positivity, diffuse Pit-1 staining, and a Ki-67 index below 2%. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge posed by silent somatotroph adenomas, underscores the limitations of biochemical assessment alone, and reinforces the essential role of histopathology and immunohistochemistry in establishing a definitive diagnosis. Long-term endocrine and neurosurgical surveillance is strongly recommended given the potential for phenotypic transformation to a functioning acromegaly syndrome.

candidates.title: Pacing Rate Acceleration in Right-Sided Heart Failure: Insight From an On-Off-On Clinical Course.
candidates.abstract: Treatment options remain limited for patients with right-sided heart failure (RHF) and severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR). Whether higher heart rate is beneficial in patients with RHF remains unclear. A 74-year-old woman with RHF and severe TR experienced marked hemodynamic and symptomatic improvement after increasing her permanent pacing rate from 60 to 90 beats/min. At 3 months, rate reduction to 60 beats/min provoked symptom recurrence within 3 days; restoring the rate to 90 beats/min promptly relieved symptoms. At 6 months, left ventricular ejection fraction remained preserved and right ventricular size remained reduced, although TR remained severe. This case suggests that increasing the pacing rate may optimize right-sided heart hemodynamics and improve symptoms in selected patients with RHF, although further validation is needed. An on-off-on response to pacing-rate adjustment-symptoms improving with higher rates and worsening at lower rates-supports a potential beneficial effect of heart rate elevation in selected patients with refractory RHF.

candidates.title: Acinetobacter baumannii Nosocomial Meningitis Secondary to Neurosurgical Intervention: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Nosocomial meningitis is a serious complication of neurosurgical procedures, associated with high morbidity and mortality, as well as significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Among the causative pathogens, Acinetobacter baumannii (A. baumannii) is particularly concerning due to its ability to survive for prolonged periods in the hospital environment, its opportunistic virulence, and, especially, its tendency to develop multidrug resistance to antimicrobial agents. Diagnosis is often difficult in the postoperative setting, particularly when the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is altered as a result of the surgical procedure. Rapid identification of the causative agent and early initiation of appropriate antibiotic therapy are essential to limit complications and improve patient prognosis. We report the case of a 27-year-old patient with a history of surgically treated craniopharyngioma complicated by anterior hypopituitarism. Three weeks after surgery, he was admitted to the ICU with suspected postoperative meningitis due to the onset of behavioral disturbances associated with nasal discharge, without a fever. Brain CT was normal. CSF analysis, obtained by lumbar puncture under strict aseptic conditions, revealed a turbid fluid with leukocytosis of 5,760 cells/mm³, predominantly composed of neutrophils, along with elevated protein levels (5.7 g/L) and low glucose levels (0.05 g/L). Direct examination after Gram staining showed Gram-negative coccobacilli with a marked inflammatory reaction. CSF culture grew a multidrug-resistant (MDR) strain of A. baumannii, which was sensitive only to colistin. The patient received antibiotic therapy with colistin, administered intravenously and intrathecally for 18 days, with initial neurological improvement and sterilization of the CSF by the 15th day of treatment. The subsequent course was unfavorable, marked by the development of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) secondary to ventilator-associated pneumonia caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), complicated by refractory septic shock, which ultimately led to his death after one month of hospitalization in the ICU. This report highlights the severity of nosocomial meningitis caused by MDR A. baumannii and underscores the importance of implementing infection prevention measures in healthcare settings.

candidates.title: From Trauma to Tumour: Incidental Giant Left Adrenal Myelolipoma in Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia.
candidates.abstract: Adrenal myelolipomas are rare, benign tumours composed of mature adipose and haematopoietic tissue. Patients with congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) are predisposed to their development, with chronic adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) hypersecretion secondary to impaired cortisol synthesis thought to be the principal driver of myelolipoma formation in this population. A 49-year-old female with known CAH presented to the emergency department following a stab wound to the abdomen. Computed tomography (CT) incidentally identified a 12 cm encapsulated left adrenal lesion consistent with a giant myelolipoma. Despite reported adherence to hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone replacement therapy, persistently elevated adrenal steroid precursors and plasma renin levels suggested suboptimal glucocorticoid control. Following multidisciplinary team (MDT) review, the patient was offered a left adrenalectomy given the lesion size (>10 cm) and concerns regarding the risk of spontaneous haemorrhage. This case underscores the importance of systematic imaging review beyond the primary indication for scanning, and the value of optimising biochemical monitoring and considering adrenal imaging in selected high-risk CAH patients.

candidates.title: Sinonasal and Olfactory Quality of Life Following Endonasal Transsphenoidal Surgery for Pituitary Adenoma: A Multicenter Prospective Cohort Triphasic Recovery Analysis in Ethiopia.
candidates.abstract: To characterize the sinonasal and olfactory quality of life (QoL) trajectory. A multicenter prospective cohort study was conducted on 91 patients undergoing TSS at Addis Ababa University teaching hospitals between May 2024 and August 2025. QoL was evaluated using the Sino-Nasal Outcome Test (SNOT-22) questionnaire v4 preoperatively and at 3- and 6-month postoperatively. Analysis revealed a characteristic triphasic recovery pattern: low preoperative baseline, a transient peak in morbidity at 3 months, and an improvement toward baseline by 6 months for most systemic domains. At 3 months, significant score worsening occurred for loss of smell/taste (mean: 1.7, p < 0.001), thick discharge (mean: 1.0, p < 0.001), congestion (mean: 1.0, p < 0.001), postnasal discharge (mean: 0.7, p < 0.001), and runny nose (mean: 0.5, p = 0.003). By 6 months, persistence was confined to loss of smell/taste (p < 0.001), thick discharge (p < 0.001), and congestion (p = 0.005). Exploratory analysis in the nasoseptal flap cohort (n = 3) showed higher scores. Preliminary findings of delayed ear pain/fullness in acromegaly at 6 months hypothesized to reflect a link between growth hormone normalization and altered Eustachian tube function. Poorer sleep with binostril access (p = 0.017) speculatively associated with bilateral synechiae under limited postoperative care. Unlike Western cohorts, protracted recovery may reflect lack of standardized high-volume saline irrigation and scheduled debridement. TSS demonstrates a favorable long-term QoL profile; however, localized sinonasal and olfactory deficits often persist at 6 months.

candidates.title: Adrenal Collision Tumors: A Practical Application of the Existing Evidence.
candidates.abstract: Adrenal collision tumors (ACTs) are rare lesions in which two histologically distinct tumors coexist within the same adrenal gland. They are almost always incidental findings, and although their heterogeneous, dual-component appearance can raise concern for malignancy, they seldom represent a distinct clinical problem. The principal pitfall they create is radiologic rather than biochemical: the mixed composition of an ACT renders the adrenal CT washout protocol unreliable and can mimic a neoplasm. The established adrenal incidentaloma pathway (biochemical exclusion of pheochromocytoma and adrenocortical carcinoma, imaging phenotyping, and size- and growth-based surveillance) reliably identifies both a functional and a malignant component of a collision tumor . Drawing on institutional experience and the published case literature, this narrative review describes the entity and its imaging caveats, and shows how the standard pathway can be applied to risk-stratify low-risk lesions and avoid unnecessary surgery while selecting appropriate first-line imaging.
candidates.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists

candidates.title: PCCT and IVUS-NIRS for High-Risk Plaque Management.
candidates.abstract: High-risk coronary plaque may be underrecognized in patients with atypical symptoms and negative biomarkers. Advanced coronary imaging can add anatomical and prognostic information. A 59-year-old woman presented with acute chest pain, mild ischemic electrocardiographic changes, and negative high-sensitivity troponin. Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) showed a predominantly noncalcified, lipid-rich-appearing plaque in the left anterior descending artery despite a low risk profile. Angiography confirmed significant stenosis, and intravascular ultrasound with near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) demonstrated a high-risk plaque phenotype with maximum lipid core burden index over 4 mm of 347. Percutaneous coronary intervention used distal drug-coated balloon treatment and proximal-to-mid drug-eluting stent implantation. Postprocedural imaging confirmed adequate stent expansion and lower NIRS lipid signal. This case highlights the complementary role of PCCT and intravascular imaging for identifying and managing vulnerable coronary plaque. PCCT for noninvasive plaque characterization and intravascular ultrasound-NIRS for intraprocedural guidance provide a complementary strategy for personalized management of vulnerable coronary plaque.

candidates.title: A Case of MEN 2A Syndrome With Bilateral Recurrent Pheochromocytoma: A Case Report and Literature Review.
candidates.abstract: Pheochromocytoma is a neuroendocrine tumor arising from chromaffin cells and producing catecholamines. Due to the excessive release of catecholamines, these tumors can present with paroxysmal episodes of high blood pressure, headache, diaphoresis, and palpitations. We present the case of a 23-year-old female patient who presented to the clinic with a history of headache, palpitations, and vomiting for two months. She was admitted for further investigations and management. Laboratory studies revealed elevated urinary and plasma catecholamine levels. Further work-up revealed bilateral adrenal masses diagnosed as pheochromocytoma and medullary thyroid cancer. The patient was diagnosed with multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN) type 2 and underwent bilateral laparoscopic adrenalectomy and total thyroidectomy with central and lateral neck dissection, and during surveillance, she was found to have recurrent pheochromocytoma. We also discuss the diagnosis and management of recurrent pheochromocytoma in MEN syndrome.

candidates.title: Clinical Interactions Between Antiseizure Medications and Direct Oral Anticoagulants: A Scoping Review on Therapeutic Failures and Knowledge Gaps.
candidates.abstract: Antiseizure medications (ASMs) are often coprescribed with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs). The pharmacokinetic (PK) interactions between ASMs and DOACs may result in altered exposure to anticoagulants, potentially increasing the risk of thromboembolic events or bleeding. This review summarizes the clinical evidence on drug-drug interactions between ASMs and DOACs. In accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines, a systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed (up to November 2025). All clinical reports and observational datasets reporting the concomitant use of at least 1 ASM and DOAC were included. ASM-DOAC combinations, PK findings, and reported clinical outcomes are presented. Thirty studies were included. Most reports involved enzyme-inducing ASMs (carbamazepine, phenobarbital, primidone, and oxcarbazepine), which were consistently associated with subtherapeutic DOAC plasma concentrations and severe clinical failures. Doubling the DOAC dose did not prevent these events in several cases. Rivaroxaban and apixaban were the most frequently described DOACs, whereas clinical data for edoxaban were limited. Evidence of non-enzyme-inducing ASMs, such as levetiracetam and valproic acid, was limited. Although enzyme-inducing ASMs compromised DOAC efficacy, the available clinical evidence was fragmented and prone to publication bias. The observed variability in interactions involving noninducing ASMs such as levetiracetam underlines the clinical complexity that may exceed theoretical PK predictions. Given the unpredictability of these interactions and the failure of empirical dose adjustments, a standardized approach for therapeutic drug monitoring and prospective, comparative trials are essential to guide personalized therapy in this high-risk population.

candidates.title: Pegvisomant in severe, treatment-resistant thyroid eye disease: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Teprotumumab, a monoclonal antibody against the IGF1 receptor, has proven effective in the treatment of thyroid eye disease (TED). Pegvisomant reduces IGF1 levels through selective inhibition of growth hormone receptors. Here, we present a hypothesis-generating case of a 69-year-old patient with progressive TED. Pegvisomant 20 mg was administered daily for 90 days. IGF1 levels declined and remained low-normal during treatment. Clinical activity scores and VISA (vision, inflammation, strabismus and appearance) scores improved rapidly. MRI assessment showed that water content of both extraocular muscles and orbital connective tissue decreased after treatment. 99mTc-DTPA SPECT confirmed the decrease in disease activity. Further studies may confirm the efficacy of pegvisomant in TED. A 69-year-old female patient with severe, active thyroid eye disease (TED) – a condition linked to Graves’ disease where the body’s immune system attacks tissues around the eyes – presented with bulging eyes (proptosis), double vision, eye redness, swelling and reduced visual sharpness.Prior treatments with standard therapies for TED, including intravenous steroid courses, radiation therapy targeting the orbit (eye socket) and the biological drug rituximab, failed to achieve improvement. TED progresses in part because proteins called IGF1 receptors on the surface of eye-socket tissues are overactivated. The researchers hypothesized that using pegvisomant, which is a medication typically used for acromegaly (hormone imbalance) that lowers insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1) levels in the blood, would reduce activation of these receptors and ease eye inflammation.The patient received a daily 20 mg injection of pegvisomant for 90 days. Symptom improvement The patient experienced a rapid reduction in eye pain, redness and swelling, alongside marked improvement in visual sharpness and colour vision within 8 weeks.MRI and imaging results Orbital MRI and nuclear imaging showed a distinct drop in tissue inflammation and fluid accumulation (oedema) in the muscles around the eye.Proptosis and double vision Eye bulging and double vision did not significantly change during the trial.Safety Pegvisomant was well tolerated with no reported side effects, and her blood sugar and liver function remained stable. Blood IGF1 levels dropped as expected and returned to normal after treatment ended. Pegvisomant rapidly reduced eye inflammation and improved vision in a patient whose TED had resisted standard therapies. However, because this was a single case study, the delayed effects from previous treatments cannot be entirely ruled out. Further clinical trials are needed to determine if pegvisomant is effective at higher doses or when given earlier in the disease course.

candidates.title: Dual therapy with tofacitinib and steroids for acute severe ulcerative colitis: a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial.
candidates.abstract: One-third of patients with acute severe ulcerative colitis (ASUC) fail intravenous corticosteroids. We evaluated whether adding tofacitinib to corticosteroids reduces treatment failure in ASUC. In this single-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, adults with ASUC were randomized 1:1 to tofacitinib (10 mg three times daily for 3 days, then twice daily) or placebo for 5 days alongside corticosteroids. Primary outcome was treatment failure at day 6 (<3-point Lichtiger reduction or total score ≥10, or colectomy). Secondary outcomes were relapse (≥3-point rise with total ≥10), rescue therapy, and colectomy at 90 days. Modified intention-to-treat analysis was performed. (CTRI/2022/11/047186). Of 62 randomized patients, 58 were analyzed: 33 in the tofacitinib arm and 25 in the placebo arm. The trial was terminated early because of slow recruitment and did not reach the planned sample size of 98. Day 6 treatment failure was numerically lower with tofacitinib in unadjusted analysis (24.2% vs 36.0%; RR 0.67, 95% CI 0.30-1.51; P = .33) and significantly lower after adjustment for baseline covariate imbalance (adjusted RR 0.47, 95% CI 0.24-0.93; P = .03). At 90 days, colectomy rates were similar (12.1% vs 12.0%; P = 1.0), but more tofacitinib-treated patients remained on assigned therapy (84.4% vs 54.2%) and rescue therapy was lower (HR 0.27, 95% CI 0.09-0.78; P = .01). Serious adverse events occurred in one versus three patients. No deaths occurred with tofacitinib versus two deaths with placebo. Dual therapy with tofacitinib and steroids in ASUC did not significantly reduce treatment failure at day 6, unless adjustment for baseline imbalance in serum albumin was taken into account. It reduced the need for rescue therapy over 90 days without affecting colectomy risk. Larger clinical trials are required to confirm these findings.

candidates.title: Medullary thyroid carcinoma with pheochromocytoma and cystic parathyroid degeneration in a ret-negative patient: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A (MEN2A) is a rare autosomal dominant hereditary cancer syndrome, predominantly caused by mutations of the RET proto-oncogene on chromosome 10q11.2. It typically presents with medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), pheochromocytoma, and primary hyperparathyroidism. Cases with a MEN2A phenotype but negative RET testing are uncommon, posing challenges for diagnosis and patient management. We report the case of a 63-year-old female who was diagnosed with MTC and pheochromocytoma. and cystic parathyroid gland. Genetic workup was negative for RET proto-oncogene mutations but positive for a heterozygous variant in the TMEM127 tumor suppressor gene. MEN2A is associated with pathogenic germline variants in the RET proto-oncogene in approximately 95-99% of cases. Our patient, however, exhibited a MEN2A-like clinical phenotype in the absence of an identifiable RET mutation, with a pathogenic TMEM127 variant instead. Although TMEM127 is an established susceptibility gene for pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma, its association with the broader MEN2A phenotype remains unclear. This unusual genotype-phenotype discordance raises important questions regarding the potential role of alternative genetic pathways in MEN2-like syndromes and creates uncertainty regarding postoperative surveillance and the appropriate extent of screening and genetic counseling for family members. Our case represents an unusual scenario where the patient presents with a clinical phenotype of MEN2A but is RET negative and positive heterozygous for a variant in the TMEM127. This atypical genetic finding introduces complexities in determining the appropriate follow-up protocol and the scope of familial screening necessary.

candidates.title: The Effect of Digital Storytelling on the Anxiety of Patients with Pituitary Adenoma Undergoing Transsphenoidal Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial.
candidates.abstract: Patients with pituitary adenoma often experience anxiety due to hormonal changes and the stress associated with transsphenoidal surgery. Digital storytelling, as an innovative multimedia-based training method, has recently been used in patient education. This study investigated the effect of digital storytelling on the anxiety of patients with pituitary adenoma undergoing transsphenoidal surgery. This randomized controlled trial was conducted on 70 patients with pituitary adenoma scheduled for transsphenoidal surgery at a teaching hospital affiliated with Tehran University of Medical Sciences. Participants were randomly assigned to an intervention or a control group. The intervention group received a 15-20-minute digital storytelling program that included experiences shared by patients and nurses regarding preoperative and postoperative care, while the control group received routine hospital education. Anxiety levels were measured a day before surgery, a day after surgery, and three weeks later using Spielberger's State Anxiety Scale. Data were analyzed by SPSS-25 software using descriptive and inferential statistics. The mean score of anxiety in the intervention group decreased by 12.45 (1.24) units a day after the surgery and by 24.82 (1.32) units three weeks after the surgery compared to baseline (p < 0.001). A significantly lower anxiety level was observed in the intervention group at both post-intervention time periods compared to the pre-intervention time (F = 17.05, p < 0.001). Repeated measures Analysis of Variance confirmed a significant interaction between time and group (F = 25.31, p < 0.001). Digital storytelling was effective in reducing anxiety among patients with pituitary adenoma undergoing transsphenoidal surgery and may serve as a valuable educational intervention.
candidates.journal: Iranian journal of nursing and midwifery research

candidates.title: Perianal fistulizing Crohn's disease increases infliximab clearance and causes low infliximab exposure (ATLANTIC).
candidates.abstract: In perianal fistulizing Crohn's disease (PFCD), higher infliximab (IFX) serum concentrations are associated with improved outcomes. PFCD patients frequently require dose intensification to reach recommended therapeutic targets. IFX pharmacokinetics (PK) in PFCD have not been previously characterized. We hypothesized that drug clearance (CL) is increased in PFCD compared to luminal Crohn's disease (LCD). Patients with PFCD and LCD starting standard-dose intravenous IFX (5 mg/kg at weeks 0, 2, and 6, thereafter every 8 weeks) were enrolled. At every visit, serum samples were collected until week 52 to measure IFX trough levels (TL) and anti-drug antibodies. A population PK model was constructed using nonlinear mixed-effects modeling and adjusted for clinically relevant covariates. A total of 148 patients were included (62 PFCD, 86 LCD) with 756 serum samples analyzed. IFX PK was described by a two-compartment model with linear elimination. After adjusting for dose, weight, serum albumin, and anti-drug antibodies, population PK modeling revealed a 23% increase in IFX CL among patients with progressive perianal fistulas during the first 14 weeks (P = .007). During induction, recommended target IFX TL was achieved in fewer PFCD than LCD patients (43% vs 57%, P = .04). At week 14, PFCD patients had lower median IFX TL than LCD (2.9 vs 4.8 μg/mL, P = .02), with fewer PFCD patients reaching phenotype-specific target TL (9% vs 46%, P < .001) compared to LCD. The presence of perianal fistulas increases IFX CL in patients with Crohn's disease, resulting in significantly lower and frequently subtherapeutic serum concentrations after standard induction dosing.

candidates.title: Long-term efficacy and safety for the complement factor B inhibitor iptacopan in IgA nephropathy.
candidates.abstract: Iptacopan, a factor B inhibitor, targets alternative complement pathway overactivation, a key driver of glomerular inflammation in IgA nephropathy. In the phase 3 APPLAUSE-IgAN trial (NCT04578834), iptacopan significantly slowed kidney function decline versus placebo over 24 months (difference in total estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] slope: 3.02 ml/min per 1.73 m2 per year [95% confidence interval (CI) 2.02, 4.01; P < 0.001]). Patients who completed APPLAUSE-IgAN or the phase 2 iptacopan trial (NCT03373461) could enter an open-label rollover extension program (REP) (NCT04557462). Patients in this REP receive oral iptacopan 200 mg twice daily alongside supportive care. Patients from the phase 2 trial were not included in efficacy analyses. Overall, 194 and 174 patients from the APPLAUSE-IgAN iptacopan and placebo arms, respectively, entered the REP. In patients who received iptacopan for up to 48 months, the total annualized eGFR slope was -3.49 ml/min per 1.73 m2 per year (95% CI -4.17, -2.80). Urine protein-to-creatinine ratio from first morning void (UPCR-FMV) reduction was sustained through 48 months with iptacopan (geometric mean ratio to baseline: 0.61 [95% CI 0.50, 0.75]). Before receiving iptacopan, the total eGFR slope over 24 months in APPLAUSE-IgAN placebo arm patients who entered the REP was -5.29 ml/min per 1.73 m2 per year (95% CI -6.09, -4.49). After switching to iptacopan, the total eGFR slope improved to -2.11 ml/min per 1.73 m2 per year (95% CI -3.08, -1.13) over the next 24 months. UPCR-FMV decreased after switching (geometric mean ratio to baseline at month 48: 0.74 [95% CI 0.59, 0.91]). Long-term safety up to 5 years (median treatment duration: 29.9 months) was consistent with the known profile of iptacopan. Long-term treatment with iptacopan led to sustained slowing in eGFR decline and proteinuria reduction that were also observed after switching from placebo. No new safety signals were observed. Registered at ClinicalTrials.gov with study numbers NCT04578834 (APPLAUSE-IgAN), NCT03373461 (phase 2 trial of iptacopan in IgAN), and NCT04557462 (rollover extension program).

candidates.title: Differences in SARS-CoV-2 rapid diagnostic testing usage by COVID-19 vaccination status can bias vaccine effectiveness estimates against symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection from a test-negative design.
candidates.abstract: Use of rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) may bias vaccine effectiveness (VE) estimates from test-negative design (TND) studies. We conducted individual-level simulations using national, US COVID-19 surveillance data to assess potential bias at varying likelihoods of visiting a healthcare facility and prevalence of RDT use. Twenty-one scenarios that varied the probabilities of visiting a healthcare facility and RDT use by vaccination status were simulated. VE was calculated as 100 × (1 - odds ratio), comparing the odds of symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection between vaccinated and unvaccinated groups of people. VE estimates were compared to VE estimates from simulations without RDT testing to calculate the bias in percentage points (pp). VE was underestimated when either vaccinated people were more likely (probability of .5) than unvaccinated people (probability of .3) to visit a healthcare facility after a positive RDT [-5.8%age points (pp); 95% uncertainty interval (UI): -9.1, -2.4] or unvaccinated people were more likely than vaccinated people to visit a healthcare facility after a negative RDT (bias = -6.1 pp; UI: -9.9, -2.5). Conversely, VE was overestimated when either vaccinated people were more likely than unvaccinated people to visit a healthcare facility after a negative RDT (bias = 5.2; UI: 2.4, 7.7) or unvaccinated people were more likely than vaccinated people to visit a healthcare facility after a positive RDT (bias = 8.4 pp; UI: 5.6, 11.3). VE estimates against symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection from a TND may be under- or overestimated, depending on differences in RDT usage between vaccination groups.
